questions.q: What separates information from story, in this lesson's essay?
choices: Information is true and stories are invented
Information comes explained and loses value once it's no longer new; a story keeps its force
Stories must be verified; information needn't be
Information follows a three-act structure
questions.explain: Benjamin says a story doesn't expend itself and can release its force long after.

questions.q: Herodotus tells how a captured king wept for an old servant but not for his own children, and doesn't say why. Why does Benjamin admire this?
choices: Because it obeys the unity of action
Because the reversal coincides with a recognition
Because it shows the value of a clear nut graf
Because leaving it unexplained keeps readers thinking for millennia
questions.explain: Keeping a story free from explanation is, for Benjamin, half the art of storytelling.

questions.q: A features editor adds a final paragraph spelling out what a narrative story 'means'. What would Benjamin say?
choices: Explanation turns a story back into information; trust the reader
Good: every story needs a controlling idea
Good: the reader needs a resolution that answers the lede
Move the explanation to the top as a nut graf
questions.explain: The storyteller leaves the reader free to interpret.

questions.q: Where does Benjamin say the storyteller's material comes from?
choices: Archetypes shared by all cultures
Research in archives
Experience, his own or other people's, passed on to listeners
The author's unconscious desires
questions.explain: He takes it from experience and makes it the experience of those who listen.

questions.q: Why does Benjamin use returning First World War soldiers as an emblem?
choices: They told the first modern war stories
They came home with less communicable experience, not more
They invented the newspaper report
They demanded realism in fiction
questions.explain: For Benjamin, experience had fallen in value and could no longer easily be shared.

questions.q: How does Benjamin characterize the novel compared with the story?
choices: As born of the solitary individual, who can no longer give or receive counsel
As a carrier bag holding many things in relation
As a readerly text consumed passively
As the oldest form of storytelling
questions.explain: The story is told in company; the novel is written and read alone.

choices: A legal warning attached to a news report
The theme stated early in a screenplay
An answer to the reader's problem
A suggestion about how a story might continue, woven into a tale
questions.explain: Counsel isn't a solution; it's practical wisdom carried by the story.

ideas: It is half the art of storytelling to keep a story free from explanation.
News is worth something only while it is new, but a story keeps its strength and can release it centuries later.
Soldiers came home from the Great War silent, poorer rather than richer in experience they could share.
The storyteller borrows his authority from death.
